instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 requires that no person may engage in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and §13.63 requires licensure for anyone receiving economic consideration for lobbying duties.
A lobbyist license issued under §13.63(1)(a) expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, meaning licenses are renewed on a biennial (24-month) cycle.

The lobbyist must obtain a separate license under §13.63, the principal must file a separate registration statement under §13.64, and §13.65 additionally requires a separate written authorization for each lobbyist-principal pairing — three distinct filings rather than one combined form.

Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the license application requirements (social security number, signature, fee) and does not require a photograph; no other section of the statute imposes a photograph requirement.

Section 13.621(3) ("Performance of public official duties") expressly exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that a state agency filing a statement under §13.695 (and named officials) are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 except as provided in §13.695, substituting a lighter agency-specific reporting regime for the standard lobbyist/principal regulations.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The statute requires principals to provide written notice before lobbying in new areas/agencies under §13.64(3) (no specific day count for changes to lobbyist registration) and §13.695(2) imposes a 10-day change notice on state agencies, but no specific deadline is set in the statute for a lobbyist to report changes to their own registration information.

Wisconsin law requires a lobbyist to be licensed BEFORE engaging in lobbying (§13.66 — "no person may engage in lobbying as a lobbyist unless the person has been licensed"), not within a number of days after first lobbying. The statute does not establish a post-lobbying registration grace period for lobbyists (the 10-day $500 threshold in §13.64 applies to principals, not lobbyists).
